svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: macOS · Gallery · item view · a preview · importing the originals from a device nearby · 1310×800
svg.desc: Mirrors the preview page's status card AS PROGRESS OF AN IMPORT FROM A DEVICE NEARBY in the Mac's Gallery item view (nearby originals, docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §7; new 2026-09-28, drawn from the code): after 'Import and Continue' for Light (gallery.item.preview.prompt.nearby.svg; drawn here on a project PicPlace holds as well, that prompt's three-button case, as tile 8's pill says) — or the card's own 'Import originals from iPhone 18 Pro' (gallery.item.preview.nearby.svg) — `PicPlaceController.importNearby` runs in the download's task slot and reports into the same `picplace.progress[id]`, phase .downloading, with `progress.source` naming the device (NearbyOffer.deviceName — the other device's DeviceName.current); so EditorPreviewPage.status answers it first, in the `.downloading` branch's import words: glyph `.cloud(.downloading)` — icloud.and.arrow.down.fill in LL.accent (§16: amber = moving; a download's own cloud); title 'Importing \(noun.text)' → 'Importing the originals' (one line: 143.1 of the 188.5 pt beside Stop); the caption 'From \(source) · \(bytesDone) of \(bytesTotal)' plus, with a resume group, ' · \(group) opens when \(pronoun) \(verb) here' → 'From iPhone 18 Pro · 486,2 MB of 1,16 GB · Light opens when they are here', three lines in the 188.5 pt column (CoreText: 183.1 · 173.8 · 44.8); under it ProgressView(value: 0.419).tint(LL.accent), 2 pt below the caption — macOS 26's bar as gallery.item.preview.downloading.svg measured it (a 20 pt frame, an 8 pt track at black 6 % across the column, the 6 pt fill inset a point); the action 'Stop' 13 pt semibold LL.accent → picplace.cancelSync, which cancels the import's task (and drops resume): what landed stays, and the next press asks only for what is still missing. 298 × 110 at y 237: 12 + title 16 + 3 + the caption's three lines 42 + 3 + the bar's 2 + 20 + 12, each Text frame rounded up to the whole point. OTHER CAPTIONS (the same seat): before the first byte 'From iPhone 18 Pro · 1,16 GB to import' (two lines, the card 96 pt — the ' · Light opens …' rides only the 'of' line); before the sending device has listed the files 'Asking iPhone 18 Pro for the files…' (two lines, 96 pt); an import started by the card's own button has no group, so no ' · Light opens …'. Non-blocking, like a download: the inspector, the filmstrip and ← → all still work, and moving on leaves the import running; the sending device has to stay open (N3). THE FILMSTRIP'S TILE 8 wears holdings-pill.there.downloading (grey camera · amber ↓ — the cloud is .downloading whoever sends), drawn over the strip component as the downloading mirror draws it: the grey camera is a project PicPlace holds as well (the prompt's alsoOnPicPlace case — Import and Continue still goes to the device nearby first, N12); importing originals PicPlace lacks (gallery.item.preview.nearby.svg's state), the camera is slashed beside the same amber ↓, and no component draws that pill yet. When the last file lands (checkArrival), PhotoViewerView replaces the page in this column with the Light panel open (EditorPageRequest.group → the editor's pendingPanel) — the rail becomes gallery.item.interval.svg's with Light open. Everything else as gallery.item.preview.svg. THE ITEM VIEW is gallery.item.svg's — the inspector column (GalleryPreviewPanel .inspector, 330 pt), the item header (▤ · ‹ Gallery · the name · 'n of N'), the editor column (the media beside the fixed 330 pt rail) and the filmstrip under everything, the floating tab bar — and GalleryItemEditor (App/GalleryItemView.swift) puts EditorPreviewPage in the editor's place when the focus request's asset is `.preview`: GalleryView.enterItem / move(to:) / step stage every project with `stageEditor(for:page:allowsPreview: true)`, so a preview opens, and the filmstrip and ← → walk straight through previews (they stalled on one until 2026-09-25). The page is its own view (EditorPreviewPageContent, plan T6), built from the editor's components with a `locked` state — never the editor mounted on a poster, so it has no write path (no persist net, no white migration, no as-shot reads). SAMPLE: tile 8 of gallery.svg's grid — the interval drawn there with holdings-pill.there.safe (a preview: its originals removed here, PicPlace holds them, the ✓ stays) — 8 of 14, an unnamed shoot, so its displayTitle is the dated 'Stack 7. 9. at 21:40' (the window title and the header both carry it); 214 JPEG originals (3024 × 4032 — INFO's Size), 1,16 GB recorded in assets.ndjson; the grade is a record, so the dots of Presets and Light still show. LAYOUT (App/EditorPreviewPage.swift railBody, the Mac's only dressing): the picture pane — black, the whole 648 × 568 column (no timeline strip, no full-screen button, no marquee badge: the badge is the dark card's) — with poster.jpg as it is (previewPictureURL; graded when it was made, never graded again), scaledToFit and centred: 426 × 568 at x 462; a Divider; the rail, a ScrollView padded 14 / 16 / 20 with 12 between — RailTabBar (App/RailTabBar.swift, locked: Text · Frames · Masks accent at 38 %, Editor selected), EditorGroupBar (.macCard, locked: every cell #6D6D72 at 42 %, none selected, the dots LL.accent at 55 %), then statusCard(style: .light) at y 237 — LL.cardBackground, radius 16, padding 12, no badge. Every greyed control stays clickable and ASKS (a click on a locked page → ask(.tab), a group → ask(.group), the card itself → ask(.line), subject 'Editing' — only while it offers Download or nothing, not while it shows Stop). macOS rounds each Text frame up to the whole point (measured: the stage-1 captures' cards are 57 and 85 pt, exactly the rounded sums), so the rest card is 85 pt where the unrounded arithmetic says 83.7. HOOKS: the nearby bench (docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §12): a Mac scratch root (`-storage.libraryRootPath`) holding the preview — a pulled project, or `LL_DROP_SOURCES=<uuid>:originals` — and a Simulator holding the originals, both bound to one picplace.test account (`LL_PICPLACE_TOKENS` always, one token per install) and, before the server hands out the key, given the same `LL_NEARBY_KEY`; then `LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid>` on the Mac with LetsLapse open on the Simulator; then `LL_PREVIEW_PROMPT=light` and `~/Library/Developer/LetsLapseRun/tools/ax press <pid> '*' AXButton 'Import and Continue'` (the hook's own ':download' presses only a PicPlace offer); `LL_NEARBY_IMPORT=<uuid>` presses the card's button instead (no resume group, so no ' · Light opens …'). The bench's Simulator sends over loopback in a fraction of a second (plan §15), so a Mac capture of this card wants a real device sending over Wi-Fi. The Mac copy needs Local Network permission (System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Local Network): refused, its browser and listener report NoAuth and the card never offers. Drawn from the code, not from a capture: a Mac importing is not benched yet (plan §15 — the Mac bench copy had no Local Network access). The words and glyphs are the code's; the card's seats are SwiftUI's own layout of statusCard's structure with these words, run offscreen on this Mac (the same structure gives the rest card 85 and the download 96, as gallery.item.preview.svg and gallery.item.preview.downloading.svg have them); the wraps are CoreText's at the column widths.
svg.text: macOS · Gallery · item view · a preview — the card as progress, importing the originals from a device nearby · 1310×800 pt window
mirrors EditorPreviewPage status (progress.source) + statusCard(.light) — Stop · Import and Continue on the nearby bench
